passages.text: By the end, you may find yourself more attuned to the cracks where trust seeps out, and more ready to ask what keeps truth alive.
Last week, in When AI Sounds Certain, Ask for Doubt, many of you explored how hesitation reshapes an answer. Some of your reflections appear at the end of this post.

What unsettled me was not the lie itself but the surface of plausibility. The headline felt familiar, echoing real claims I have seen before. I noticed how easily I wanted to believe it, and how little effort it took for the tool to make it.
Sitting with that discomfort reminded me how quickly belief can form, and how much slower it is to question, cross-check, and resist the pull of the easy answer.
By practising slowness here, you rehearse what it means to pause before passing something on. You practise the small acts of attention that help resist manipulation and protect trust.
#### **From Last Week: When AI Sounds Certain, Ask for Doubt**
> BD shared a dialogue with ChatGPT that began with the question “Are tree leaves green?” and unfolded into a meditation on perception, context, and truth.
> Hodman Murad noted that the most valuable lesson may not be how AI gives us answers, but how it reminds us to sit with uncertainty.
> L. Elaine Dazzio spoke of doubt as permission, a gentler rhythm that lets us admit we do not always need to know at once.
These reflections show how doubt can be more than a pause, it can be a practice that shapes how we think and decide together.
If you try this week’s prompt, I would love to see the most unsettling fake your tool created. I read and respond to all your comments.
